decisionsTitle: The calendar keeps its «Filtre» slot in every month
decisionsSection:
**What failed.** CI on the BR-V2.42 batch (2026-09-30): `event-pages.spec.ts` — «changes month without moving the controls or reflowing the grid» — measured the «Luna următoare» arrow 44 px lower on a phone and 60 px lower on a desktop after the click. The review suspected the header (the menu order of §571 read differently on the static calendar and on its live twin, §549). The trace says otherwise: every header node after the click is the same DOM node as before it, apart from the current entry's state. What was new was in `<main>`. The static calendar, this month, had no «Filtre» panel. The live twin's next month had one.

**Why it showed that day.** §413 gave the calendar the listing's rule: with nothing to narrow and nothing ticked, the panel does not render. A box is offered only when some of the period's events carry a value and not all do. On 2026-09-30 September's only seeded event left in the month was the past Sunday's run, so there was nothing to choose between. October had a race, a trail run and a road run, so it had something. The seed dates its events from today, so the test goes red on any day when one of the two months it steps between offers nothing and the other does. A reader sees the same thing: a month change puts a 44-pixel button above the arrows they have just pressed. BR-REQ-041-01 criterion 12 says the calendar's controls do not move when the month changes. So the panel's slot may not depend on the month.

**Decision.** On the calendar the panel is always rendered, inside `CalendarFilterSlot` (`events/ui/CalendarFilterSlot.tsx`). With nothing to offer and nothing ticked, the slot holds it with `visibility: hidden`. This is the same markup, so the box is the same height at every width. It is out of the accessibility tree, the tab order and the pointer, so what §413 wanted still holds: a button that opens onto no boxes is not offered. The listing keeps §413's rule, because its panel does not change under a pressed control: a filter or a page load changes the listing, never a pair of arrows on it.

*Rejected:*
- Changing the header. It was not the cause, and it renders the same on both pages.
- Reading the offer off something wider than the month on view (the upcoming rows, the adjacent months). The panel would then offer boxes that do not narrow what is shown, which §413 refuses.
- Moving the panel under the arrows. It would change the page's layout to fix a height.
- Loosening the test. It measured a real jump.

**Tests.** Unit `events/calendar-filter-slot.test.ts` renders the slot both ways. The held slot has the panel in its markup with `visibility: hidden` and never `display: none`, and the calendar page draws its panel through the slot and nowhere else. A new e2e test in `event-pages.spec.ts` makes the criterion independent of the date. A January two years back has nothing to offer; its slot is held, has the closed panel's 44-pixel height, and puts the arrow where the calendar's own month puts it. Both Playwright projects run it on a production build.
changelogLine: - **The calendar's arrows stay put** — a month with nothing to filter keeps the «Filtre» button's room, unseen, so stepping into a month that has filters no longer pushes the arrows down under your thumb. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the calendar, when the month on view offers no filter and nothing is ticked, then the «Filtre» panel is still in the page, held unseen (`visibility: hidden`: out of the accessibility tree, the tab order and the pointer) in a box of the closed panel's height, so the calendar's controls sit at the same height in a month with filters and in one without (2026-09-30, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the calendar keeps its «Filtre» slot in every month
